fields.meta_title: Product Launch Landing Page Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a product launch landing page from a prompt, with a countdown, reminder emails, launch pricing, and signups in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Product Launch Landing Page Before Launch Day
fields.hero_description: Get a product launch landing page that counts down to your launch hour and saves every signup to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Launch Page Needs on Launch Day
fields.features_subheading: A launch page has two jobs: build a list before the hour and turn visitors into users after it. These six parts cover both.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt, a working launch page

Tell Emergent what the product does, who it is for, and when it goes live. It builds the page, its form, and the signup table, and changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
A page that changes at the launch hour

Before launch, visitors see a countdown and a form to get reminded. At the hour you set, the page shows the action they can take now, and each person who asked gets an email.
fields.feature_3:
Every signup as a row you own

Each signup is saved with its source link and answers. Built apps connect to any tool with an API, so a new row can update a contact in HubSpot instead of a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_4:
Slack alerts for the signups that matter

Pick a rule, such as a team of 20 or more or a signup through a partner's link. Each signup that matches posts to Slack or sends an email to the person who owns the follow-up.
fields.feature_5:
A count to watch on launch morning

The dashboard behind the page updates as each signup arrives. Split it by source to see which post or email brings in the most people during the first hours after launch.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, the code later

Publish on your own domain, which is included and uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, ready to grow into the product's main site.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Product Launch Landing Page Examples
fields.tab_content_1:
Countdown until 10 AM ET, then a download button

Pellucid, a screen recorder for Mac, launches on Tuesday at 10 AM ET. Until then, its page shows a countdown and a Remind me form, and 3,214 people left an email. At 10 AM the countdown gives way to the download button, and each of the 3,214 gets the reminder email.
fields.tab_content_2:
No campaign date until 2,500 people subscribe

Fernhollow makes cast-iron camp stoves and will not set a crowdfunding date until 2,500 people subscribe to its pre-launch page. Each subscriber picks the stove size they would back. The counter updates live: at 1,874 subscribers, 1,122 have picked the large stove and 752 the small one.
fields.tab_content_3:
$19 a month holds for anyone who signs up within 72 hours

Tallyhook sells bookkeeping software for food trucks and opened with a founding price. Anyone who signs up within 72 hours of launch keeps $19 a month; after that, the page shows $29. A clock on the page counts down the window. Marisol Quintavalle signed up at hour 70, and her row saved $19.
fields.tab_content_4:
Oriel Banfield hears about salons of 3 or more groomers

Marrowby, scheduling software for dog groomers, launched text reminders to current customers on one page. Each signup adds a reminders tag to the customer's HubSpot contact. Salons of 3 or more groomers also send account manager Oriel Banfield a Slack message. Tidewater Grooming signed up with 5 groomers.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Product Launch Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to publish a product launch landing page that collects signups early and switches over at your launch hour.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the hour the page changes
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for an email and one choice
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the launch day, the hour, and the time zone, and write all three on the page. A visitor in another time zone should be able to work out when to come back without asking. If the date can still move, say what has to happen first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write one headline for before launch and one for after. The first says what is coming and asks for an email; the second says the product is live and names the one action to take. Keep the product name the same in both.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for an email and at most one question whose answer changes what you do on launch day, such as plan size or the version someone wants. Cut any field you would not act on before the first week is over.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the hour and both headlines into one prompt, with the form fields. Emergent builds the page with its countdown and the signup table behind it. Prompt again for anything that reads wrong, such as the confirmation screen visitors see.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Connect your email tool and Slack
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the email tool that sends the reminders, then Slack for the signups you want to hear about. If sales follows up after launch, map new signups to your CRM now instead of copying rows across by hand later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Rehearse the switch with a test time
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set the launch hour to 10 minutes from now on a copy of the page. Sign up with two test addresses, wait for the switch, and check that the new button shows and both reminder emails arrive. Then set the real hour back.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page at least a week before launch, while there is still time for people to hear about it and sign up. Share the link with the people who will spread it on launch day, and give them the launch hour too.

faq_plan.q: What are the 7 steps to launch a new product?
faq_plan.ref: What are the 7 steps to launch a new product?

prov.original: What are the 7 steps to launch a new product?

faq_plan.a: The seven steps are to name the buyer, test demand, set a price, pick a date, recruit people to share it, launch, and follow up. Test demand with a product launch landing page before you build much: signups at a stated price tell you more than opinions do. Keep the page up after launch, since late visitors still arrive from every link you shared.

faq_plan.q: How to create a product launch?
faq_plan.ref: How to create a product launch?

prov.original: How to create a product launch?

faq_plan.a: Create one by working back from a fixed launch date and hour. Put up a page that says what is coming and collects emails, then write the announcement and the reminder email before launch week starts. Describe that page to Emergent's AI landing page builder with the launch hour and the form fields, and it builds the page with a signup table behind it.

faq_plan.q: What is the best way to launch a product?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best way to launch a product?

prov.original: What is the best way to launch a product?

faq_plan.a: The best way is to launch to people who already asked for it. Build a list in the weeks before, announce to that list first, and post publicly an hour or two later, once the first users have tried it. Signups on a page built with Emergent sit in a database you own, and the same list is there for the next launch.

faq_plan.q: What are the phases of a product launch?
faq_plan.ref: What are the phases of a product launch?

prov.original: What are the phases of a product launch?

faq_plan.a: A product launch has three phases: pre-launch, launch day, and follow-up. In pre-launch you build interest and a list. On launch day the product opens and the announcement goes out. In follow-up you answer the people who came and fix what they ran into. Once the launch is over, turn the launch page into a standing product landing page for visitors who arrive later.

faq_plan.q: What is a good message to launch a new product?
faq_plan.ref: What is a good message to launch a new product?

prov.original: What is a good message to launch a new product?

faq_plan.a: A good launch message says in one line what is now available and who it is for, then gives one action with a date or a price attached. For example: Pellucid is live, a screen recorder for Mac that turns any recording into a link you can send, and you can download it today. Cut anything that does not help the reader decide whether to click.

faq_plan.q: What should I copy from Kickstarter landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Copy their pre-launch setup: a page that shows the product before the campaign opens and asks for one click to hear about the launch. Kickstarter says it will send a launch notification email to your followers when your project goes live. That list becomes your day-one traffic. Put the reward and its price high on the page, where a visitor reads them first.

faq_plan.q: What should a launch landing page include after launch day?
faq_plan.a: After launch day, it should include the action people can take now up top, such as a download or a free trial, and drop the countdown and the reminder form. Keep the launch date as a line of proof that the product is new. If the product is a phone app, rework the page as an app landing page with store buttons and screenshots.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a launch form include?
faq_plan.a: A launch form should include an email field plus, at most, one question you will act on, such as team size or the plan someone wants. Every extra field costs signups on a page whose job is to build a list. Forms built with Emergent have no response cap: a launch that brings in 10 times the expected signups keeps every one.

faq_plan.q: How do I announce a new product launch?
faq_plan.ref: How do I announce a new product launch?

prov.original: How do I announce a new product launch?

faq_plan.a: Announce it to your list first, by email at the launch hour, then post on the channels where your buyers spend time. Lead with the product and the one action to take, and link to the launch page. The FTC's CAN-SPAM guide says your message must include your valid physical postal address. Put it in the footer of every launch email.

faq_plan.q: How to do a successful product launch?
faq_plan.ref: How to do a successful product launch?

prov.original: How to do a successful product launch?

faq_plan.a: Do a successful product launch by picking a date early, building a list before it, and rehearsing the launch hour once. Open the page on a phone before launch day, because a link shared in a text or a social app opens there. A mobile landing page with one large button gives that visitor a clear next step. Then put your time behind the links that bring in signups.

plan.angle: The top 10 is example galleries (Unbounce, Dribbble, Behance, Canva), two builder blogs and a crowdfunding listicle; none shows what a launch page does on the hour it goes live. This page shows four launch pages working: a countdown that switches to a download button at a set hour, a crowdfunding pre-launch list with a subscriber goal, a founding price that holds for 72 hours, and a feature launch to current customers synced to a CRM. The FAQ answers the launch questions searchers ask: steps, phases, the message, the announcement. Waitlist, coming soon, product and app landing pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
